latest_release.body:
### Added

* A borrowed number, `bool`, `char` or borrowed string crosses by copy, so
  `&f64`, `&Option<T>`, `&Nullable<T>`, `Option<&f64>` and
  `Option<&Nullable<T>>` are argument types, and an
  `experimental_generic_mono` import taking `&T` accepts `T = f64`,
  `Option<f64>` or `Nullable<String>`, as std's `contains(&T)` does.
  [#5436](https://github.com/wasm-bindgen/wasm-bindgen/pull/5436)

* Added a rejection type parameter to `js_sys::Promise<T, E = JsValue>`,
  mirrored on `JsFuture<T, E>`, `PromiseState<T, E>` and
  `PromiseWithResolvers<T, E>`. Awaiting a `Promise<T, E>` yields
  `Result<T, E>`, converting the rejection reason as an `E` the same unchecked
  way the fulfilled value is converted as a `T`. Both parameters are covariant
  under `Upcast`; `catch`, `then_with_reject` and the `withResolvers` reject
  function receive an `E`; `all_tuple` / `all_settled_tuple` carry a shared `E`
  through; and under `js_sys_unstable_apis`, `Promise::new`, `Promise::reject`
  and `Promise::any` are typed on the rejection too, `any` as
  `AggregateError`. The default keeps existing `Promise<T>` code unchanged.
  `PromiseWithResolvers<T, E>` is invariant in both, since its `resolve` and
  `reject` functions take them, and `JsFuture<T, E>` is `UnwindSafe` whenever
  `T` and `E` are.
  [#5426](https://github.com/wasm-bindgen/wasm-bindgen/pull/5426)

* Added the `--js-string-builtins` CLI flag, importing `static_string`
  constants as [JS String Builtins](https://github.com/WebAssembly/js-string-builtins)
  string constants from `wasm:js/string-constants` instead of defining them in
  the JS glue. With reference types, `static_string` constants now occupy
  fixed `externref` table slots filled in when the module is instantiated, so
  cloning and dropping them is free and never calls into JS.
  [#5401](https://github.com/wasm-bindgen/wasm-bindgen/pull/5401)

* Added `Nullable<T>`, re-exported as `js_sys::Nullable`, for a `T | null`
  value at the JS boundary, as `Option<T>` is for `T | undefined`, with
  `Option<Nullable<T>>` for `T | null | undefined`. Both are accepted wherever
  `Option<T>` is, for every `T` and in every position: JS `null` is
  `Nullable::Null` and is sent back as `null`, while `undefined` into a plain
  `Nullable<T>` goes to `T`'s own conversion. A plain `Option<T>` still reads
  both `undefined` and `null` as `None` and writes `None` as `undefined`; the
  `Option` layer of `Option<Nullable<T>>` treats only `undefined` as `None`,
  since `null` has to reach the `Nullable` layer. `Option<T>` converts from
  and into `Nullable<T>`, and
  `JsNullable<T>` converts from both and into `Option<Nullable<T>>` for
  `T: JsGeneric`.
  The API follows `Option`'s, including `ok_or`, `and_then`, `filter`,
  `as_deref`, `take`, `replace` and `IntoIterator`, and
  `--cfg wasm_bindgen_unstable_try_trait` enables `?` on nightly.
  `NullableIntoWasmAbi` / `NullableFromWasmAbi` carry `Nullable<T>`'s `null`
  for every `T`, and are supertraits of `JsStringLike` and the js-sys
  primitive-union markers, so `Nullable<impl JsStringLike>` and
  `Nullable<impl JsNumberOrStringLike>` work under `experimental_generic_mono`,
  and `Nullable<T>` erases like `Option<T>` on a generic import.
  [#5410](https://github.com/wasm-bindgen/wasm-bindgen/pull/5410)
  [#5423](https://github.com/wasm-bindgen/wasm-bindgen/pull/5423)

* `Nullable<T>` converts into `JsValue` with `From`, `Null` becoming `null`
  as `None` becomes `undefined` for `Option<T>`, and `Option<T>`,
  `Nullable<T>` and `Result<T, E>` are `Promising` for any `T: Promising`,
  so a `Promise<Nullable<JsString>>` awaits to a `Nullable<JsString>`.
  `String` and `&str` upcast to `JsValue`, and `String` to itself, so a
  `Promise<String>` from an `experimental_generic_mono` import is `JsGeneric`
  and upcasts to `Promise<JsValue>` as `Promise<bool>` does. Together these
  make a `Promise<Nullable<JsString>>` or `Promise<String>` from a mono
  import usable wherever a promise is expect

detail.readme:
wasm-bindgen

Facilitating high-level interactions between Wasm modules and JavaScript.

Guide (main branch) | API Docs | Contributing | Chat

Built with 🦀🕸 by The Rust and WebAssembly Working Group
## Install `wasm-bindgen-cli` You can install it using `cargo install`: ``` cargo install wasm-bindgen-cli ``` Or, you can download it from the [release page](https://github.com/wasm-bindgen/wasm-bindgen/releases). If you have [`cargo-binstall`](https://crates.io/crates/cargo-binstall) installed, then you can install the pre-built artifacts by running: ``` cargo binstall wasm-bindgen-cli ``` ## Example Import JavaScript things into Rust and export Rust things to JavaScript. ```rust use wasm_bindgen::prelude::*; // Import the `window.alert` function from the Web. #[wasm_bindgen] extern "C" { fn alert(s: &str); } // Export a `greet` function from Rust to JavaScript, that alerts a // hello message. #[wasm_bindgen] pub fn greet(name: &str) { alert(&format!("Hello, {}!", name)); } ``` Use exported Rust things from JavaScript with ECMAScript modules! ```js import { greet } from "./hello_world"; greet("World!"); ``` ## Features * **Lightweight.** Only pay for what you use. `wasm-bindgen` only generates bindings and glue for the JavaScript imports you actually use and Rust functionality that you export. For example, importing and using the `document.querySelector` method doesn't cause `Node.prototype.appendChild` or `window.alert` to be included in the bindings as well. * **ECMAScript modules.** Just import WebAssembly modules the same way you would import JavaScript modules. Future compatible with [WebAssembly modules and ECMAScript modules integration][wasm-es-modules]. * **Designed with the ["Web IDL bindings" proposal][webidl-bindings] in mind.** Eventually, there won't be any JavaScript shims between Rust-generated wasm functions and native DOM methods. Because the Wasm functions are statically type checked, some of those native methods' dynamic type checks should become unnecessary, promising to unlock even-faster-than-JavaScript DOM access. [wasm-es-modules]: https://github.com/WebAssembly/esm-integration [webidl-bindings]: https://github.com/WebAssembly/proposals/issues/8 ## Guide [**📚 Read the `wasm-bindgen` guide here! 📚**](https://wasm-bindgen.github.io/wasm-bindgen/) ## API Docs - [wasm-bindgen](https://docs.rs/wasm-bindgen) - [js-sys](https://docs.rs/js-sys) - [web-sys](https://docs.rs/web-sys) - [wasm-bindgen-futures](https://docs.rs/wasm-bindgen-futures) ## MSRV Policy * Libraries that are released on [crates.io](https://crates.io) have a MSRV of v1.81. * CLI tools and their corresponding support libraries have a MSRV of v1.86. The project aims to maintain a 2-year MSRV policy for libraries (meaning we support Rust versions released within the last 2 years), but with a shorter MSRV policy for the CLI. Changes to the MSRV may be made in patch versions, and will be logged in the CHANGELOG and MSRV history below. ### MSRV History | Version | Library MSRV | CLI MSRV | Date | |---------|--------------|----------|------------| | 0.2.129 | 1.81 | 1.86 | 2026-09-23 | | 0.2.118 | 1.77 | 1.86 | 2026-04-10 | | 0.2.106 | 1.71 | 1.82 | 2025-11-27 | | 0.2.103 | 1.57 | 1.82 | 2025-09-17 | | 0.2.93 | 1.57 | 1.76 | 2024-08-13 | ## License This project is licensed under either of * Apache License, Version 2.0, ([LICENSE-APACHE](LICENSE-APACHE) or http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0) * MIT license ([LICENSE-MIT](LICENSE-MIT) or http://opensource.org/licenses/MIT) at your option. ## Contribution **[See the "Contributing" section of the guide for information on hacking on `wasm-bindgen`!][contributing]** Unless you explicitly state otherwise, any contribution intentionally submitted for inclusion in this project by you, as defined in the Apache-2.0 license, shall be dual licensed as above, without any additional terms or conditions.
